critical_finding.summary: The OECD Competition Assessment Reviews: Logistics Sector in ASEAN (2021) is the strongest multilateral publication found. However, it explicitly and repeatedly cites Mordor Intelligence (2020) as the source for ALL ASEAN freight and logistics market revenue figures including the USD 357.78B (2019), USD 481B (2025 projection), and the road freight share data. The OECD report does not independently originate or validate these commercial figures — it simply incorporates them. This means the entire chain of ASEAN logistics market revenue claims ultimately traces to a single commercial aggregator (Mordor Intelligence), regardless of whether the intermediary citing it is the OECD or another party.
critical_finding.one_independent_data_point: The OECD report does contain one calculation using 'road freight transport revenue' as an input: USD 46.44B for road freight in 2019 across three ASEAN member states (those for which data were available for the OECD's benefit-calculation exercise). This figure is embedded in a welfare-analysis calculation (p. 114 of PDF, line 5809 of markdown) and is not itself a full-ASEAN market sizing — it covers only the subset of countries where recommendations applied.
critical_finding.government_statistics_gap: Indonesia BPS publishes Land Transportation Statistics 2022 and 2023, which cover road lengths, vehicle counts, accident data, and railway transport — but NOT freight market revenue in IDR/USD. These are physical-stock statistics, not value-of-market statistics.
critical_finding.itf_oecd_transport_outlook: The ITF Southeast Asia Transport Outlook (Oct 2023) exists as a primary OECD/ITF publication but the PDF returned 403 Forbidden. The OECD landing page was also 403 Forbidden. Tagged NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH.

partial_evidence_note: The OECD (2021) publication, while secondary for market-sizing purposes, does provide corroborating qualitative structure: road freight is ~64.6% of total ASEAN freight transport revenues (2019), and freight transport is ~72.6% of total logistics revenues (2019). If those structural ratios are applied to any independently-obtained logistics total, the derived road-freight figure would have stronger grounding. However, no independent logistics total was found.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: [ASSUMED-N]: ASEAN road freight market is approximately $119B (2025E); ASEAN all-modes logistics market approximately $288B (2025E); Indonesia road freight approximately $54B (2025E) — figures sourced from Mordor Intelligence, which is the ultimate data origin even where cited by OECD secondary publications. To validate: commission cross-check against ITF Southeast Asia Transport Outlook (2023) and Indonesia Ministry of Transportation revenue data.

ASEAN all-modes logistics market is estimated in the range of USD 280–360B (2025E), based on commercial market research (Mordor Intelligence); no independent primary government or multilateral source was found that independently validates this figure. Road freight is estimated at approximately 40–65% of total freight transport revenue based on OECD-cited structural ratios.
suggested_revision_options.rationale: Range reflects structural ratio uncertainty and single-source risk

If the artifact requires a primary-sourced figure, the specific $119.43B / $288.2B figures cannot be substantiated from any source other than Mordor Intelligence (directly or via OECD secondary citation). Consider replacing with qualitative framing: 'ASEAN logistics is one of the largest freight markets in Asia, with logistics costs accounting for approximately 5% of regional GDP (OECD, 2021)' — this OECD-originated fact is reliable.

oecd_citable_fact.fact: Logistics currently accounts for about 5% of ASEAN GDP and provides approximately 17 million jobs
oecd_citable_fact.note: This fact is directly stated in the OECD-authored foreword and repeated in the body — it is OECD's own finding, not citing Mordor Intelligence. It can replace or complement the Mordor market-size figures as a grounded anchor.

reasoning: After 10 WebSearches and 5 WebFetch/markitdown operations across six primary-source categories (ADB, OECD/ITF, World Bank, UNESCAP, Indonesia BPS, ASEAN Secretariat) and three consultancy categories (McKinsey, BCG, Roland Berger), no source that independently originates or cross-validates the $119B ASEAN road freight or $288B ASEAN all-modes logistics figures was found. The strongest multilateral publication in the space (OECD 2021 Competition Assessment) itself cites Mordor Intelligence for those figures. The claim remains single-source (Mordor Intelligence) and should be marked ASSUMED-N. One OECD-originated fact IS available as a strong anchor: logistics = ~5% ASEAN GDP. Four potentially useful sources were blocked (403) and are tagged NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH.
